page.layout: One printed page with a running head above the text and a catchword at the lower right. The text is one column of running text in full width. No marginal notes. The sliver of the neighbouring page at the right edge is not transcribed.

main_text.p: sionis[?] Adami. v. 14. in quorum numero, si non soli, ceteræ præcipui sunt illi infantes, qui ante usum Rationis morientes, nullius actualis peccati rei esse potuerant per ætatem; at interim geniti erant, intra Sethi post lapsum, ad imaginem & similitudinem primi Parentis. Quinimo, & experientia quotidiana satis demonstrat, cæteras Pœnas, quæ iunt peccati solitus effectus, in omne Genus humanum exinde redundasse. Neque hinc Injustitiæ, aut nimiæ Rigoris Deus ullo modo argui poteft, cum nihil ufitatius sit in statu civili, quam ut Perduellio parentum aliudve quovis gravioris notæ flagitium, posteris imputetur, etsi nondum natis, in Dedecus & Damnum totius Familiæ. Legimus item, quod Achanis Sacrilegium, & Davidis Crimen in agendo censu totius Israelis, celeriter in damnum integræ Reipublicæ; & Principis erratum toti populo imputabatur in Pœnam. Cæterum Adamus, non solum totius humani Generis princeps erat, ratione dignitatis & Regiminis, sed & parens Communis ratione naturæ, utpote, in cujus lumbis totum delituit, & ut loquitur Damascenus, [illegible, ~12 letters] virtute quadam seminali continebatur. Unde & Apostolus alibi ait, sicut in Adamo omnes moriuntur, sic & in Christo omnes vivificabuntur. 1 Cor. 15. 22.

Secundo; Imaginem istam Divinam & similitudinem Dei, ad quam Homo primum creatus est, post peccatum in eo remansisse. Soc: Prælect: Cap. 3. Smalc: cont: Frantz: Disp: 7. Ad quod probandum duo potissimum S. Scripturæ loca adducunt, viz. Gen. 9. 6. Jac. 3. 9. in quibus Homo, post lapsum, dicitur factus ad imaginem & similitudinem Dei. Nos è contra, etsi fateamur istam Imaginem Dei in Homine, in qua ab origine conditus est, non penitus •

page.notes: The first word is a fragment at the start of the page, read as "sionis" with the long s and a doubtful first letter. The Greek phrase after "Damascenus," could not be read and is marked illegible. The dot after "penitus" is a printed reference mark with no matching note on this page. The running head is read with a doubtful word ("sana"). "Prælect" and "Quinimo" are partly blurred. The text "deletam" is the catchword below the last line. "Leginus" in the scan reads as "Legimus". The printed text reads "iunt" and "solitus" in "quæ iunt peccati solitus effectus" as printed. A possible printing error: "ufitatius" for usitatius, kept as printed. The right page edge is not part of this page.
